descriptionChirho: To physically pull, draw out, or extract an object or person from a place, such as pulling someone from a pit or drawing water; the basic Qal sense of exerting force to move something toward oneself.
To draw, attract, or entice a person figuratively, often used of God drawing people to himself with lovingkindness or of romantic attraction; implies relational influence rather than physical force.
To drag, haul, or pull away by force, often with a connotation of violence or compulsion, as in dragging away the wicked or hauling iniquity with cords.
To extend, stretch out, or prolong in time or space, including extending patience or forbearance, stretching out a boundary, or prolonging a duration.
Passive forms indicating something is prolonged, delayed, or deferred, whether in the Nifal stem (shall-be-prolonged) or Pual participle (deferred, as of hope deferred).
Pual participial use describing people as tall, stretched out, or of extended stature; a descriptive adjectival sense derived from the passive of stretching.
To draw out or prolong a sound, specifically the blast of a ram's horn (shofar/yobel); a specialized sense of extending the duration of a musical note.
To draw or handle a weapon, especially a bow, describing warriors who draw the bow or wield arms in battle.
To scatter or sow seed, a specialized agricultural sense of drawing or casting seed across the ground; used of the sower in a farming context.
